244:
A. Location. No adult entertainment establishment shall be located:
1. Within one thousand (1,000) feet of any parcel of land that falls within any of the following zoning districts as defined by the zoning ordinance of the city of Sparta and the official zoning map of the county: R-1, R-2, R-2a, C-1, or C-2;
2. Within one thousand (1,000) feet of any parcel of land on which a church, school, college campus, public park or children's day care facility is located;
3. Within five hundred (500) feet of any parcel of land upon which any establishment authorized to sell alcoholic beverages or malt beverages and wine for consumption on the premises is located;
4. In any zoning district other than an I industrial district; or
5. Within one thousand (1,000) feet of any parcel of land upon which another adult entertainment establishment regulated or defined hereunder is located.
For purposes of this section, distance shall be by airline measurement from property line, using the closest points on the property lines of the parcels of land involved. The term "parcel of land" means any quantity of land capable of being described by location and boundary, designated and used or to be used as a unit.
B. Adult Entertainment Establishment Employees.
1. Qualifications. Employees of an adult entertainment establishment shall be not less than eighteen (18) years of age. No employee employed as an adult entertainer shall have been convicted of an offense described in subsection 5.30.050(d)(3) of this chapter within the five (5) years immediately preceding the proposed employment at or by an adult entertainment establishment. Any adult entertainer who is convicted of any such crimes while employed as an adult entertainer shall not thereafter work on any licensed premises for a period of five (5) years from the date of such conviction, unless a longer time is ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction. The term licensed premises shall mean the premises where an adult entertainment establishment for which a license is obtained pursuant to this chapter operates, conducts or carries on its business. The term convicted shall include an adjudication of guilt or a plea of guilty or nolo contendere or the forfeiture of a bond when charged with a crime in a court of competent jurisdiction.
2. Permit for Employment. Before any person may work as an adult entertainer on a licensed premises, as defined in subsection (B)(1) of this section, he or she shall file a notice with the city clerk of his or her intended employment on forms supplied by the city clerk and shall receive a permit for such employment from the city clerk. The prospective employee shall supply a signed and notarized consent, on forms prescribed by the Georgia Crime Information Center, authorizing the release of his or her criminal records to the city police department. The prospective employee shall also provide a list of all of his or her convictions of offenses described in subsection 5.30.050(d)(3) herein (including pleas of nolo contendere) within the past five (5) years. The city clerk shall approve or deny the permit within fifteen (15) days of the application. If the prospective employee is found to meet the requirements of this subsection, and upon payment of the permit fee, the city clerk shall issue a permit approving such employment within forty-eight (48) hours. Upon receipt of a permit, the employee may begin working on the licensed premises. If approval is denied, the city clerk shall provide the prospective adult entertainer the reasons for the denial and the prospective employee may, within ten (10) days of said denial, appeal to the city council which shall uphold or reverse the decision within thirty (30) days of such appeal. If the city clerk does not approve or deny an application for a license within forty-five (45) days of the date such application was received by the city clerk, then on the expiration of the forty-fifth day: (a) the application shall be approved and the city clerk shall immediately issue the license for which application was made, and (b) the applicant shall have the right to begin operating in the manner allowed by the license for which application was made. The annual permit fee shall be twenty-five dollars ($25.00).
3. Suspension or Revocation of Permit—Procedure. Violation by an adult entertainer of the provisions of this chapter and/or conviction of an offense described in subsection 5.30.050(d)(3) of this chapter shall subject an adult entertainer to suspension or revocation of the permit for employment. Whenever the city clerk finds that reasonable grounds exist to suspend or revoke a permit for employment issued hereunder, the city clerk shall schedule a hearing before the city council to consider such action and shall notify the employee at least twenty (20) days prior to the hearing of the time and place of the hearing and the proposed action and grounds therefor. The employee shall be entitled to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses with or without legal counsel. The city council shall make its decision within ten (10) days of the hearing and shall notify the employee promptly in writing. In the event that a permit for employment is suspended on revoked by the city clerk, a fifty dollar ($50.00) appeal cost shall be assessed against the permit holder.
4. Independent Contractors. For the purpose of this chapter, independent contractors working as adult entertainers shall be considered as employees and shall be required to satisfy the provisions of this chapter relating to employees of adult entertainment establishments, regardless of the business relationship with the owner or licensee of any adult entertainment establishment.
C. Hours of Operation. An adult entertainment establishment may be open only between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m.
D. Display of Licenses. An adult entertainment establishment licensee shall conspicuously display the license required by this chapter.
E. Performance Area. All dancing by adult entertainers at adult entertainment establishments shall occur on a platform intended for that purpose which is raised at least eighteen (18) inches from the level of the floor.
F. Lighting. All areas of an adult entertainment establishment licensed hereunder shall be fully lighted at all times patrons are present. Full lighting shall mean illumination equal to 3.5 footcandles per square foot.
G. Covering of Windows and Doors. All adult entertainment which is licensed and permitted by this chapter shall be carried on inside a closed building with all windows and doors covered so that the activities carried on inside cannot be viewed from the immediate areas surrounding the outside of the building.

245:
A. Advertising Without License. No person, partnership, corporation or other entity shall advertise or cause to be advertised an adult entertainment establishment without a valid adult entertainment establishment license issued pursuant to this chapter.
B. Employment of Minors or Unpermitted Persons. No adult entertainment establishment licensee shall employ or contract with a person under the age of eighteen (18) years or an adult entertainer who has not obtained a permit pursuant to this chapter.
C. Sale, Consumption of Alcohol. No adult entertainment establishment licensee shall serve, sell, distribute or suffer the consumption or possession of any alcoholic beverages, malt beverages or wine or controlled substance upon the premises of the licensee.
D. Contact Between Patrons, Employees. No dancing or other performance by an adult entertainer at an adult entertainment establishment shall occur closer than four (4) feet to any patron. No patron, customer or guest shall be permitted to touch, caress or fondle any specified anatomical area of or any part of the body or clothing of any adult entertainer. No patron shall directly pay or give any gratuity to any adult entertainer. No adult entertainer shall solicit any pay or gratuity from any patron.
E. Engaging in Specified Sexual Activities Prohibited. No adult entertainer, other employee, patron or other person at an adult entertainment establishment shall be allowed to engage in any specified sexual activity as defined herein on the premises of any adult entertainment establishment.
F. Public Indecency Prohibited. No adult entertainer, other employee, patron or other person at an adult entertainment establishment shall, while on the premises of an adult entertainment establishment, commit the offense of public indecency as defined in OCGA Section 16-6-8.

249:
A. Grounds.
1. A license may be denied to persons or entities that have submitted an incomplete application or that have failed to satisfy any of the requirements of the city's ordinance regulating adult entertainment establishments found at Sections 5.30.010 through 5.30.160 of this chapter.
2. Any of the following shall be grounds for suspension or revocation of a license:
a. The making of any statement on an application for a license issued hereunder which is material and is later found to be false;
b. Violation of any of the regulations or prohibitions of this chapter;
c. With respect to the applicant, operator(s) and owner(s), conviction of or a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to any of the crimes which would make such person or adult entertainment establishment ineligible to hold a license under Section 5.30.050(D) above.
B. Denial—Procedure. Within thirty (30) days of actual receipt of an application for an adult entertainment establishment license, the city clerk shall either approve or deny the application. In no event shall the city clerk's decision whether to approve or deny the adult entertainment establishment license application be withheld for more than thirty (30) days after actual receipt of the application. In the event that such an application is held without decision for a period of more than thirty (30) days, however, the license application shall be deemed approved, and expressive conduct may begin immediately notwithstanding the fact that no license has been issued. The city clerk shall issue an adult entertainment establishment license to an applicant who informs the city clerk of the fact that an application has been submitted, but no decision has been made thereon for a period of more than thirty (30) days following actual receipt of the application. Notwithstanding the fact that the license provided by this sentence shall not be a prerequisite to the commencement of business operations contemplated by the application, the city clerk shall issue an adult entertainment establishment license under such circumstances within three (3) business days of actual receipt of written notice by the applicant of such circumstances. In the event that the city clerk denies an application for an adult entertainment establishment license, notice of such denial shall be delivered to the applicant in person or by certified mail within five (5) business days of such denial. Any person aggrieved by any decision of the city, its officials, employees or agents, pursuant to this article, may seek review of such decision by filing an appropriate pleading in the superior court of the county or any other court of competent jurisdiction including, but not limited to, a mandamus petition pursuant to OCGA Sections 9-6-20 through 9-6-28.
C. Suspension or Revocation—Procedure. Whenever the city clerk finds reasonable grounds exist to suspend or revoke a license issued hereunder, the clerk shall schedule a hearing with the city council to consider such suspension or revocation and shall, at least twenty (20) days prior to the hearing, notify the licensee of the time and date of the hearing and the proposed action and the grounds therefor. The licensee shall be entitled to present evidence and cross-examine any witnesses at the hearing, with or without legal counsel. The city council shall make its decision within ten (10) days of the hearing and shall notify the licensee in writing within five (5) business days of the decision.

254:
Any adult entertainment establishment having available for customers, patrons or members, any booth, room, or cubicle for the private viewing of any adult entertainment must comply with the following requirements:
A. Access. Each booth, room or cubicle shall be totally accessible to and from aisles and public areas of the establishment, and shall be unobstructed by any curtain, door, lock, or other control-type or view-obstructing devices or materials.
B. Construction. Every booth, room or cubicle shall meet the following construction requirements:
1. Each booth, room or cubicle shall be separated from adjacent booths, rooms and cubicles and any nonpublic areas by a wall.
2. Have at least one (1) side totally open to a public lighted aisle so that there is an unobstructed view at all times of anyone occupying same.
3. All walls shall be solid and without openings, extended from the floor to a height of not less than six (6) feet and be light-colored, nonabsorbent, smooth-textured and easily cleanable.
4. The floor must be light-colored, nonabsorbent, smooth-textured and easily cleaned.
5. The lighting level of each booth, room or cubicle when not in use shall be a minimum of ten (10) candles at all times, as measured from the floor.
C. Occupants. Only one (1) individual shall occupy a booth, room or cubicle at any time. No occupant of same shall engage in any type of sexual activity, cause any bodily discharge or litter while in the booth, room or cubicle. No individual shall damage or deface any portion of the booth, room or cubicle.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in the context of this ordinance, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except whereas the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abuse or cruelty to animals or fowl means knowing and willful failure by an owner, or any other person charged with an animals or fowls care, to care for that animal or foul in a humane manner, or, by act, omission or neglect, causing or inflicting unjustified physical suffering, pain, harm, or death to an animal or fowl.
Adequate food and water means food and water which is sufficient in amount and appropriate for the particular type of animal to prevent starvation, dehydration, or a significant risk to the animal's health from a lack of food or water.
(1) Adequate food means palatable, non-contaminated, and nutritionally adequate food that is fed according to the species requirements or is fed as directed by a veterinarian. Adequate food does not include garbage.
(2) Adequate water means clean, fresh, potable water offered to pets at suitable intervals according to the species requirements, or as dictated by naturally occurring states of hibernation normal for the species, or as directed by a veterinarian.
Animals means any and all types of animals, domesticated and wild, male and female, singular and plural.
Animal control officer means the chief of the Sparta Police Department or his designee.
Animal establishment means any pet shop, grooming shop, animal auction, kennel, performing animal exhibition or animal shelter, except this term shall not include veterinary medical facilities, licensed research facilities, facilities operated by government agencies or licensed animal dealers regulated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
Animal shelter means a facility designated or recognized by the city council for the purpose of impounding and/or caring for animals.
At-large means off the premises and not under the immediate control of the owner or custodian of the animal.
City council or council means the City of Sparta City Council.
Confinement/confined means kept within an electronic confinement system, building, pen or fenced area or other structure built to prevent escape by a domestic animal.
Dangerous dog means any dog, that according to the records of an appropriate authority; (1) inflicts a severe injury on a human being, domesticated animal or domesticated fowl without provocation at any time after March 31, 1989; or (2) Aggressively bites, attacks or endangers the safety of humans, domesticated animals or domesticated fowl, without provocation after the dog has been classified as a potentially dangerous dog and after the owner/custodian has been notified of such classification.
Domesticated fowl means any and all birds, male and female, singular and plural, kept as pets or kept, maintained, bred or harvested for agricultural purposes.
Feral cat means a feral cat or a stray cat is an un-owned domestic cat that lives outdoors and avoids human contact: it does not allow itself to be handled or touched, and usually remains hidden from humans.
Feral cat colony means either cats that were born and raised in the wild, or domestic cats that have been abandoned or lost and turned feral in order to survive and live in a group.
Fowl means any and all birds, domesticated and wild, male and female, singular and plural.
Guard dog or attack dog means any dog which has been trained to attack persons or other animals independently or upon verbal approval command, and any dog which, while not so trained, is reasonably expected by the owner to perform as a guardian of the property upon and within which it is located.
Humane manner means care of an animal to include at least adequate heat, ventilation, sanitary shelter, wholesome food and clean water, consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animals' size, species and breed.
Inclement weather means weather conditions likely to adversely affect the health or safety of the dog (includes rain, sleet, ice, snow, wind, extreme heat or cold, and anything else that is likely to adversely affect the well-being of the animal)
Kennel means an establishment kept for the purposes of breeding, selling or boarding more than three (3) dogs or three (3) cats, except litters of animals of not more than six (6) months of age, for commercial purposes, or engaging in training of dogs or cats for commercials purposes.
Licensing authority means the city agency or designated representative thereof charged with administering the issuance and/or revocation of permits and licenses under the provisions of this chapter.
Neutered/spayed means rendered permanently incapable of reproduction.
Nuisance means a domestic animal which:
(1) Damages, soils or defecates on private property other than the owners, or on public walks and recreation areas, unless such waste is immediately removed and properly disposed of by the owner.
(2) Causes a disturbance or annoyance to other by excessive barking or other noisemakers, or offensive odors.
(3) Chases vehicles or molests, attacks or interferes with persons, domestic animals or domesticated fowl.
Owner means any natural person or any legal entity, including but not limited to, a corporation, partnership, firm or trust owning, possessing, harboring, keeping or having custody or control of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog within the county or who knowingly permits a dog or other animal to be harbored or kept, or has a dog or other animal in is care, or who permits a dog or other animal to remain on or about the premises.
Poison means a substance that is capable of causing the illness or death of a living organism when introduced or absorbed.
Potentially dangerous dog means any dog, which without provocation bites a human being, domesticated animal or domesticated fowl at any time after March 31, 1989. No dog shall be deemed to be a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog solely on incidents in which the dog:
(1) Inflicts an injury upon a person when the dog is being used by a law enforcement officer in connection with the law enforcement officer's official duties.
(2) Inflicts an injury if the injury as sustained by a person, who, at the time, was attacking the dog's owner or the owner's family members, committing a willful trespass or other tort, or was tormenting, abusing, or assaulting the dog, or had in he past been observed or reported to have tormented, abused or assaulted the dog, or was committing or attempting to commit a crime.
Proper enclosure means an enclosure for keeping a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog confined in a manner suitable to prevent the entry of young children and to prevent the dog from escaping. A proper enclosure shall have secure sides, and a secure top; and if the dog is enclosed within a fence, all sides of the fence shall be of sufficient height and the bottom of the fence hall be constructed or secured in a such a manner as to prevent the dog's escape either from over or from under the fence. All gates shall be constructed so that they are self-closing and self-latching. A proper enclosure shall provide protection from the elements for the dog.
Records of an appropriate authority means records of any state, county, or municipal law enforcement agency, records of county or municipal animal control agency, county board of health, federal, state or local court, or an animal control officer as provided in this chapter or by the laws of the State of Georgia.
Severe injury means any physical injury that results in broken bones, death, cosmetic surgery or lacerations requiring medical treatment.
Tethering means the action of tying an animal with a rope or chain so as to restrict its movement.

267:
It shall be unlawful for any person owning or having possession or control or care of a dog to allow the dog to stray or run at large upon the streets, playgrounds, or other public places or private properties of others within the city. A dog shall at all times be restrained or enclosed upon the premises of the owner or person having the dog in care, possession, or custody, except as may be permitted under exceptions provided in this section. A dog is properly restrained when it is under the control of the owner or person having possession and held by a cord, rope, chain or similar tether. Any such restraint must be applied in a manner to protect the health and safety of the dog. A dog is properly enclosed when it is securely confined (confined defined as kept within an electronic confinement system, building, pen or fenced area or other structure built to prevent escape by a domestic animal) indoors or in a securely enclosed and locked pen, or physical or electronic fence designed and functioning to prevent the dog from escaping. Dogs classified as dangerous of vicious as defined in O.C.G.A., Title 4, Article 2 shall not be permitted to be confined by electronic fence, and shall be confined in such a manner suitable to prevent entry of young children and designed to prevent the dog from escaping. It shall be unlawful for any owner of a domestic animal to chain, tie, fasten or otherwise tether the animal to dog trees, fences, vehicles, or other stationery objects as a means of confinement except that when the animal may be temporarily confined by a tether while in physical attendance of its owner.
Electronic confinement systems shall not be considered an adequate means of confinement if the system is improperly installed, malfunctioning, in disrepair, damaged, switched off, or otherwise deactivated or nonoperational. Any domestic animal confined by means of electronic confinement system must wear at all times the appropriated and properly functioning receiving device while within the confines of the system. Signage indicating the presence of an electronic confinement system must be placed around the perimeter of the system at regular intervals in sufficient quantity and of sufficient size so as to be clearly visible by anyone approaching the property. No animal which has been classified or is currently being reviewed for classification as a dangerous, potentially dangerous, or vicious dog pursuant to state or local law may be confined by means of electronic confinement systems.
It shall be unlawful for the owner of an animal to allow it to run at large unattended on or about the streets, right of ways, and highways of Sparta; in any Sparta city park, except in any city parks that are or maybe specifically designated as off leash areas; unattended on or about the common property of any apartment complex or condominium community; or on the property of another person without permission of the owner of that property. This section shall not apply to dogs being used for hunting in accordance with state law, rules and regulations.
Every parent or head of a household where a dog is kept shall be deemed to be a responsible party under and for purposes of this section, even though others might be equally responsible with him with respect to the same dog. The fact that a dog may be owned by a minor child shall be no defense to a parent who is the head of a household.
A dog not in a vehicle and securely confined therein, when away from the premises where habitually kept, shall be on a leash and under control of a person capable of controlling the dog and protecting others against harm.
Whenever a dog is being transported in a vehicle, it shall not be taken under the vehicle or allowed to escape therefrom at any place other than where habitually kept, unless on a leash and in control of a capable person, as provided in this section. When transporting an animal in the back of a truck, it should be crated, and the crate shall be securely tied to the body of the cab bed.
Any person leading or allowing their leashed dog onto the property of another is guilty of the crime of trespassing, and can be charged in the municipal court of the city for this crime.
It shall be the responsibility of the dog owner or whoever is in charge of the dog at the time to clean up behind their dog. All litter and feces shall be removed from any public or private property immediately, and deposited in a waste receptacle. Failure to clean up behind the animal can result in a citation for littering.
This section does not prohibit persons with disabilities from bringing guide animals into any such areas or into any city park or area owned or operated by the city for recreational purposes.
Specific requirements for enclosures:
Sanitation of primary enclosures: Primary enclosures for pets must be cleaned at a frequency and intensity to provide a healthy and hygienic environment in order to prevent disease hazards. Excreta must be removed to prevent contamination of the animals contained therein and to reduce the spread of disease. Soiled bedding should be removed and replaced with fresh materials as often as is necessary to keep the animals clean and dry. For hard surfaces that are conducive to cleaning with water, frequent flushing with water and periodic use of detergents or disinfectants should be used to maintain sufficiently clean surfaces. When a hosing or flushing method is used for cleaning, animals contained in the enclosure must be removed unless the enclosure is large enough to ensure the animals would not be harmed, wetted, or distressed during the process. Animals in nearby enclosures must be protected from being contaminated with water and other wastes during the cleaning. Enclosures may be disinfected by using appropriate chemicals, hot water, or a combination of both. If hot water is used as a means of disinfection, the temperature of the water must be at least one hundred forty-five (145) degrees F. All domestic animals shall be provided with clean, potable water and adequate food at all times.
Guidelines that constitute proper housing include a permanent structure with a waterproof roof that is structurally sound, sufficiently insulated to protect the animal from the elements (rain, snow, ice, excessive cold, flooding above grade, excessive heat and excessive direct sunlight), with space to change position, stand, turn around, lie down and make all other normal body movements (allowing animal to extend to full stride) in a normal and comfortable position appropriate to the age, size and health of the animal. The structure and surrounding area need to be free from excessive dirt, trash or waste so as not to threaten the physical well-being of the dog. Examples of inadequate shelter include, but are not limited to, lean-tos, metal or plastic drums, boxes, vehicles, or the area on or beneath exposed porches or decks. Enclosure shall all for adequate exercise suitable to the age, size, species and breed of the animal, proper ventilation and elimination of mud.
It shall be unlawful for any owner of a domesticate animal not to control the animal at all times through one (1) of the following means.
(1) On a leash when off the property of the owner.
(2) Within the passenger area of a vehicle driven or parked on the streets or securely crated and tied down to a truck bed.
(3) Within the property limits of its owner and attended by the owner.
(4) Confined within the property limits of its owner or of another with the permission of the person in control of the property.
Note— Exemptions: Feral cat colony caretakers are exempt from the requirements of chapter 6.04.110 section.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
268:
It is unlawful for any person to own, possess, harbor, control, or keep on any premises any dog that barks or howls so continuously or incessantly as to unreasonably disturb the peace and tranquility of the neighborhood. Commercial dog kennels, permitted by zoning law where located, are subject to dog barking nuisance laws as well as other applicable county codes. Animal services is responsible for enforcement of the provisions of this section.
For purposes of this section, evidence that the dog has barked or howled for an aggregate period of twenty (20) minutes out of one (1) hour shall be sufficient for conviction. If the first nuisance barking or howling complaint is determined to be provoked by any other animal or nearby pedestrian(s), it may be excluded from the aggregate time if the owner: (1) provides documentation that the provocation exists and cannot be avoided; and (2) takes remedial steps to change the environment of the dog(s) and abate the nuisance within a six (6) month period from the date of the complaint.
For purposes of this section, evidence that two (2) or more dogs are provoking each other to bark, shall be sufficient for conviction under this section, so long as the barking continues for an aggregate twenty (20) minutes out of one (1) hour, regardless of which dog commenced the barking. In such instance, owners of each dog involved shall be subject to citation.
Upon receipt of any complaint based on continuous or incessant barking or howling, an animal control officer shall investigate and take a report from any complaining witness.
Upon evaluation of the report, if in the opinion of the animal control officer a valid complaint exists, the officer shall contact the owner of the animal complained about and advise the owner of the existence of the complaint, and instruct the owner to abate the nuisance.
If the owner of the dog at the time of the issuance of any citation has been convicted of a violation of this section, or has pled no contest to such violation, on two (2) or more occasions within twelve (12) months from the time of the issuance regarding the same dog, the violation(s) of this section shall be a misdemeanor.
Nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent any party from bringing a civil action to abate the nuisance.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
269:
The animal control officer, while on duty, shall seize and impound, subject to this article, all dogs found running at large upon any public highway, street, alley, court, square, park, sidewalk or any other public property within the city limits, whether in the immediate presence of the owner or custodian or otherwise, as provided in this code.
The animal control officer, while on duty, shall seize and impound, subject to this article, all dogs found running at large upon any unfenced lot, tract or parcel of land within the city limits, whether in the immediate presence of the owner or custodian or otherwise, and such animal control officer is authorized to enter upon an unfenced lot, tract or parcel of land for the purpose of seizing and impounding any dog running at large thereon, as provided in this code.
The animal control officer is empowered and authorized to enforce all aspects of this code. Further, he is authorized and empowered to issue citations to any person in violation of this code. He can cause the arrest of any person who resists the animal control officer's attempts at resolving animal caused violation.
The animal control officer shall see that all dogs that are impounded shall have sufficient amounts of water and food and shall furnish shelter from the elements. Sanitary conditions will be maintained, and dogs will be cared for in a humane manner.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
270:
Any person finding any animal upon his property may contact the animal control officer to impound said animal immediately.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
271:
The owner of an animal impounded pursuant to this chapter shall be liable for the cost of the maintenance of such animal during impoundment. Such costs shall be set forth in the schedule fees and charges on file of the city clerk and shall be payable upon redemption of such animal.
(a) Any vaccinated, licensed animal impounded may be held in the animal shelter designated by the city for a period of seventy-two (72) hours. An owner surrendered animal will be available for adoption twenty-four (24) hours following the day of surrender if all veterinary actions have been provided.
(b) The owner of any animal impounded under this chapter may redeem the animal by paying or making payment arrangements for all fines and fees within seventy-two (72) hours of impoundment.
(c) Payment arrangements shall be at the discretion of the City of Lead.
(d) After seventy-two (72) hours, the disposition of the animal shall be at the discretion of the animal shelter.
(e) Any unlicensed animal that is redeemed must also acquire an animal license in addition to paying or making arrangements for all fees and fines.
(f) An unvaccinated animal that is redeemed must also provide proof of vaccination within ten (10) days or the animal may be impounded.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
272:
Any animal impounded under this chapter or otherwise in the control of the animal control officer and not redeemed within three (3) days following the date of its impoundment, in the case of an animal without indicia of ownership or within three (3) days after the owner is notified in the case of an animal with indicia of ownership, may be disposed of by adoption or by euthanasia.
An exception may be made when:
(1) An animal is injured or sick and in the judgment of a licensed veterinarian employed by or under the control of the city council, cannot recover
(2) An animal has a documented condition that is highly contagious; or
(3) When the cost of treating such animal would be prohibitive.
In those events, the veterinarian may decide immediate euthanasia is necessary. The animal control officer shall make a prompt and reasonable effort to locate and notify an impounded animal's owner in person or by certified mail, return receipt requested. The animal control officer will make every reasonable effort to find an acceptable adoptive home for home animals in his control before considering euthanasia. No impounded animal shall be adopted until it has been given all appropriate shots and has been neutered or spayed in the case of an adult animal. An impounded animal who is available for adoption and is too young to be altered may be adopted once it has been given appropriate vaccinations and the adoptive owner has agreed in writing to have the animal neutered or spayed when said animal reaches no more than seven (7) months of age. Veterinarian charges shall be paid by the adoptive owner and such charges shall be set out in the fee schedule on file in the office of the city clerk and shall be payable upon adoption of such animal.
Records. The animal control officer shall keep accurate written records showing the intake through final disposition of all dogs and cats compounded by him/her, in which records shall be open and available for public inspection.
Adoption.
(1) The Sparta animal care and control officer may offer for adoption any animal deemed abandoned or any animal that has been surrendered by the owner.
(2) An animal may be donated (surrendered) for adoption only by a resident of Sparta, GA and may be made available for adoption upon the determination by the animal control superintendent that the animal is of reasonably good health and temperament. In the vent that the owner of an animal at the time of impound desires to reclaim an animal remaining in custody of the Sparta animal care and control, after the animal has been deemed abandoned the animal control officer may, in their discretion, permit such prior owner to adopt the animal in accordance with this section, provided however, that no dog or cat shall be adopted by the prior owner unless said animal has been spayed or neutered at the owner's expense.
(3) Potential persons who want to adopt an animal must make an application for the adoption with Sparta animal care and control and meet requirements associated with the humane housing and care for the animal as determined by Sparta animal care and control and by the payment of required fees.
(4) No unclaimed dog, which is not neutered or spayed shall be released from the Sparta animal care and control without written agreement from the person adopting the animal that such animal be sterilized within thirty (30) days of adoption. Failure of the owner to spay or neuter the adopted dog within the prescribed time will constitute a violation of O.C.G.A. 4-14-3© and will be prosecuted as a misdemeanor as prescribed in O.C.G.A. 4-14-4.
(5) Adopted animals under six (6) months of age must be sterilized by the time the animal is seven (7) months of age.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
273:
It shall be unlawful for anyone to knowingly abandon, abuse or fail to keep any domesticate animal or domesticated fowl in a humane manner within the city. Each animal so abandoned or abused and each day the violation of chapter exists shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
274:
O.C.G.A. 4-8-2 through 4-8-30 is incorporated herein by reference thereto, except as set out in this article.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
275:
It shall be the duty of each owner, tenant, or custodian of an enclosure or building within each a guard dog or attack dog, or dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog is located to conspicuously post a notice on the outside of the enclosure or building. Said notice shall have six (6) inch red or black letters on a white background and shall contain the following information "WARNING, DANGEROUS DOG". OR "WARNING POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS DOG". In the case of a building such notices shall be posted consciously upon such enclosure at a distance not greater than fifty (50) feet apart as well as upon each and every entrance and exit. In the case of apartments, condominiums or businesses located within a larger building where the guard or attack dog is located.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
276:
No person shall tether a dog to a stationary object or mobile device unless the following conditions are met: A first violation of this section shall be punished by a written warning. Subsequent violations shall be punishable by a fine of up to one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) at the discretion of the municipal judge.
(a) Tethers must allow the dog to walk at least ten (10) feet excluding the length of the dog.
(b) Tethers must have a swivel on each end to prevent twisting and tangling.
(c) Tethers must be attached to a harness or halter that is specifically made for a dog and is properly fitted for the specific dog, this harness or halter must go around the dog's body and not the neck of the dog.
(d) Tethers must be made of a material that allows the dog to freely move. For example, heavy chains such as log chains are not acceptable.
(e) The dog must not be able to reach a hazard such as a public road, porch edge, window sill, etc. that could cause an injury to the dog.
(f) The dog must have access to adequate shelter, food and water as defined in this document.
(g) The dog must not be left unattended for more than 2 continuous hours.
(h) Whenever a dog is being transported in a vehicle, it shall not be taken under the vehicle or allowed to escape therefrom at any place other than where habitually kept, unless on a leash and in control of a capable person, as provided in this section. When transporting an animal in the back of a truck, it should be crated and the crate shall be securely tied to the body of the cab bed.
(Ord. No. 248, 2-12-2019; Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
278:
No person in the city limits of Sparta shall give away any dog or cat as a charity prize or to another person prior to revising the licensing with animal control. Puppies and kittens must be registered prior to eight (8) weeks of age. State law allows for one (1) litter per calendar year. More than one (1) litter per year requires a pet dealers license.
The maximum number of cats/dogs that can be owned per household is five (5) adult animals.
(Ord. No. 257, 9-14-2021)
281:
All food establishments operating or operating within the city shall comply with all ordinances of the city and shall comply with all regulations adopted by the State Board of Health which are applicable to food service establishments, including any future amendments to such regulations or any regulations adopted in the future by the State Board of Health.
(Amended during 1997 codification: Ord. 166 § I, 1974)
282:
A. No new license shall be issued nor any licenses be renewed annually, as now required by ordinance, without an application setting forth the location of the business, together with the name and address of the owner of the business, and in addition hereto a statement of the Hancock County Board of Health, or its agents, recommending that the license be issued, together with the license fee now required by ordinance.
B. The application for a new business shall be filed and the license issued prior to the time that the business is actually open for business and all renewal licenses shall be filed and approved prior to March 15th of each year.
(Ord. 166 §§ 2, 3, 1974)
283:
Should it be determined that any food service establishment is in violation of the rules and regulations of the State Board of Health pertaining to food service establishments, which are herein adopted as the rules and regulations of the mayor and councilmembers of the city, a ten-day written notice specifying the violations complained of shall be given by the Hancock County Board of Health, or its agents, or by the chief of police, and if after ten (10) days from said written notice the violations complained of are not corrected, the same shall be a violation of this chapter, and the person or persons violating the same shall be punished as provided by Section 5.13(c) of the city of Sparta Charter.
(Ord. 166 § 4, 1974)
284:
A. Should it be determined that any person has violated the provisions of this chapter and is willfully continuing to violate the same, the chief of police is authorized and empowered to cite the person or persons in violation of this chapter, requiring them to appear before the mayor and councilmembers of the city to show cause why the license issued to said person or persons should not be revoked, which hearing shall be held at the time and place specified in said notice, at which time the mayor and councilmembers of the city shall cancel the license in question if the charges are found to be true and justify same.
B. Should any person or persons operate a food service establishment within the city without first having obtained a license, as required by this chapter, or after the license has been revoked by the mayor and council-members of the city, as herein provided, the same shall be a violation of this chapter and punishable as prescribed in the Charter of the city of Sparta.
(Ord. 166 §§ 5, 6, 1974)
286:
As used in this chapter, the following terms are defined and shall be construed as follows:
The term garbage as used in this chapter shall refer to and mean the ordinary accumulation of refuse incident to the operation of a household or place of business, and shall not be construed to include brick, stone, lumber, wood, boxes or building debris, which mentioned articles and things shall not be removed by the agencies of the city as garbage, and the same are to be removed from the premises by the owner or occupant, at his expense.
Large businesses means businesses which produce an average of not more than twenty (20) nor less than four (4) cubic yards of garbage and trash weekly.
Medium-sized businesses means businesses which produce an average of not more than four (4) nor less than one-half cubic yards of garbage and trash weekly.
Single-family dwelling means a building or any part thereof used exclusively as living quarters for any number of individuals living together as a single housekeeping unit.
Small businesses means businesses which produce an average of less than one-half cubic yard of garbage and trash weekly.
Very large businesses means businesses which produce an average of more than twenty (20) cubic yards of garbage and trash weekly.
(Ord. 159 § 1 (part), § 2 (part))
287:
Any building debris such as plaster, roofing, concrete, brickbats and other such rubbish resulting from repairs, remodeling or construction of any building or private property will not be removed by the city. The owner of the premises or the contractor, professional landscaper, builder or the person doing the repairs, remodeling or construction shall be required to haul away and dispose of all such debris, including stumps, trees and limbs.
(Ord. 159 § 1 (part))
288:
It is unlawful for any owner, occupant or tenant of any property or premises, whether vacant or occupied, or for any person, either as owner or in control of any vacant lot, to permit to remain thereon any filth, trash, weeds or noxious growth, filthy or standing water, or other unhealthful or unsightly matter.
(Ord. 159 § 1 (part))
289:
A. If any owner, tenant or other person in possession or control of any premises, within the city limits, shall fail or refuse to remove therefrom such matter as set out in Section 8.08.030, within five (5) days after having been notified so to do by the city, then and in that event, the owner, tenant or other person in possession or control of such premises, whether vacant or otherwise, shall upon conviction of violation of the provisions of said section, be subject to fine and imprisonment, all or both in the discretion of the court.
B. In case of failure or refusal of any person to comply with the provisions of Section 8.08.030, and as cumulative of the remedy hereinbefore provided by prosecution of such offenders, the city, through its proper authority, shall have the right to enter upon and remove from any such lands or premises, all weeds growing or standing thereon, and all other growth of like character, thereby placing such premises in sanitary and sightly condition, and to charge the cost of same to the owner, or owners of any such premises or vacant lots, and the clerk shall have full, ample and complete authority to issue therefore execution in the name of the city, which execution shall issue and be levied as executions for taxes in the city are issued and levied. Such execution shall issue and constitute a lien upon the property so cleaned and against the owner, or owners thereof; provided, a detailed, itemized statement of the cost of such work shall be attached to and form a part of said execution; and provided further, that no execution shall issue against any land owner unless he shall have been served in person with written notice at least five (5) days before such work is commenced by the city; and provided further, that in the event such land owner is a nonresident, such written notice must have been mailed to him, or to his last known address, at least ten (10) days prior to beginning the work by the city.
C. The owner against whom execution may have issued, as hereinbefore provided, shall have the right to contest the same, or the amount thereof, in the same manner as provided by the laws of the state governing illegalities and claims where executions are levied.
(Ord. 158 § 1 (part))
290:
A schedule of reasonable rates, tolls, fees and charges to be made against owners, occupants, tenants and lessees of buildings and premises for the service by the sanitary department or the city's contractors of collection, removal and disposal of garbage, trash and rubbish within the city shall be determined by a resolution of the city council. Said resolution shall also specify the frequency of collection and removal of garbage and trash from houses, buildings and premises used for residential, commercial, and business purposes, which frequency shall be not less than once per week. Said resolution shall be posted at the city water department and copies shall be made available to the public within a day of the adoption of said resolution. Council may adopt new rates, tolls, fees and charges and frequency of collection and removal as often as circumstances require by the adoption of successive resolutions.
(Ord. 213, 2005)
291:
A. To avoid duplication in billing and as a convenience to the public, all persons engaged in furnishing or delivering water, either by conveyance or transporting the same by containers or through the medium of pipes and connecting service, wherein a charge is made for such service, shall be required to include the fees for the service herein provided on the monthly water bills. Such persons, engaged in furnishing or delivering water, either by conveying or transporting the same by containers or through the medium of pipes and connecting service, shall as a convenience to the public, receive and issue receipts for the charges made in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, and shall promptly remit the same to the city monthly as the same assesses.
B. It is further provided that should any person or persons, owners, occupants, tenants and lessees of residential buildings and premises or business and commercial buildings and premises fail or refuse to pay the charges fixed against said owners, occupants, tenants and lessees as provided for in this chapter when due, the mayor and councilmembers shall be privileged to disconnect water services to the residential buildings and premises or business and commercial buildings and premises of said owners, occupants, tenants and lessees against such sanitary service charge or fee and charge for the collection, removal and disposal of garbage, trash and rubbish services until such fees have been paid in full. All such delinquent charges shall be collected as other claims of the city through the chief of police or such other official as may be hereafter designated by the mayor and councilmembers.
C. The city clerk or other duly authorized collector of garbage collection charges shall, after the failure of any person or entity to pay delinquent garbage collection bills and the water department has certified that other methods of collection are ineffective, place a fi. fa. on the property where service was received and shall maintain a docket on delinquent garbage collection bills which shall be available for examination. In addition to any delinquent garbage collection bills, the city clerk is authorized to charge the property owner any costs for the execution of the fi. fa. and the maintenance of the docket.
D. In all instances where the garbage collection customer is not the record owner of the property, the city clerk must mail a copy of the delinquent notice to the record owner and said record owner must be given at least thirty (30) days to resolve any delinquency before the city clerk may file a fi. fa.
E. Customers that have a past due balance after disconnection are subject to being referred to collection agencies and are required to pay for postage, second notices, collection fees, court processing fees, and attorney fees.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part); Ord. 212, 2004; Ord. 221, 2007)
292:
Any owners, occupants, tenants, and lessees of residential buildings and premises or business and commercial buildings and premises who do not receive monthly water bills shall be billed for the charges fixed and assessed by this chapter and upon failure to pay the same when due the mayor and councilmembers shall be privileged to discontinue collection, removal and disposal of garbage, trash and rubbish services until such fees have been paid in full. All such delinquent charges shall be collected as other claims of the city through the chief of police or other such official as may be hereafter designated by the mayor and councilmembers.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
293:
A. Refuse commonly known and described as garbage shall be kept in fly-proof containers at some convenient location upon the premises of the owner or occupant, where the same may be removed by the agencies of the city; provided, however, that where the premises of the occupant have no outside area accessible for the keeping of garbage before removal, the owner or occupant, may, with the written permission of the city's sanitary inspector, place near the sidewalk, a garbage can or container; provided, the same shall be of metal, shall be fly-proof, and shall be so placed and fastened as to prevent overturning. Such garbage cans as are placed on the streets, with the permission of the sanitary inspector, shall be painted of such color as the sanitary inspector shall designate.
B. All garbage cans and containers shall be subject to inspection by the city's sanitary inspector, and when, in his opinion, such can or container is no longer a suitable or sanitary receptacle for the keeping of garbage, said sanitary inspector shall notify the owner of the unsuitableness of the container and require him to meet the requirement of this chapter.
C. Merchants are required to put all small trash in bags.
(Amended 2-17-88; Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
294:
It is unlawful for any person to place upon the streets, sidewalks, lanes, alleys, or public parks of the city any refuse, wood, lumber, brick, sticks, brush, trash, leaves, paper, ashes or other debris.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
295:
A. Those designated by the mayor and serving as the sanitary committee for the city shall determine and assign the proper classification under the schedule in Section 8.08.050, and shall give notice of the same in writing to the owners, occupants, tenants and lessees of business and commercial buildings and premises and such notice shall designate a specific time in which appeal may be made regarding the initial designation and assignment under the classification schedule set forth in this chapter. Any owner, occupant, tenant and lessee disagreeing with the designated charge assessed against them by the sanitary committee shall file their objection in writing with the sanitary committee and, if after review by the sanitary committee, then said person may appeal in writing from the decision resulting from said review by the sanitary committee directly to the mayor and councilmembers and said matter shall be heard at the next regular council meeting after the date that the appeal from the determination made by review of the sanitary committee and the determination as to classification thus made by the mayor and councilmembers shall be final.
B. If there should be property, premises or buildings which would fall into two (2) or more classifications, then and in that event, it shall be the duty of the sanitary committee to determine the classification and charge for the collection, removal and disposal of garbage, trash and rubbish applicable thereto. Any owners, occupants, tenants and lessees disagreeing with such determination as made by the sanitary committee under this section shall have the same rights of appeal and appeal shall be made as provided in this section.
C. Any property not covered by this section shall be assigned and designated, such classification determining such fee or charge for the collection, removal and disposal of garbage, trash and rubbish as shall be deemed fair and reasonable to the sanitary committee. Any owners, occupants, tenants and lessees disagreeing with such determination as made by the sanitary committee under this section shall have the same rights of appeal and appeal shall be made as provided in this section.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
296:
The sanitary committee and the mayor and councilmembers shall have the exclusive right of the collection, removal and disposal of garbage, trash and rubbish and no private individual, business, agent or other operation shall be permitted to haul the garbage, trash and rubbish as produced by owners, occupants, tenants and lessees of residential buildings and premises or business and commercial buildings and premises without first having obtained permission from the sanitary committee therefore. Anyone desiring such permission shall file such application, giving the details of operation and any charges to be made all as may be required by the sanitary committee. Once a permit is issued by the sanitary committee for such operations, the same shall be issued in the name of the applicant and such permit shall not be transferable. The sanitary committee shall have full authority, to make any and all such other reasonable regulations relating to the hauling of garbage, trash and rubbish over city streets and thoroughfares by outside collectors. And all outside collectors shall have a similar right of appeal as that set forth in Section 8.08.100. Ownership of all garbage, trash and rubbish collected or deposited on the city dump shall be vested in the city.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
297:
Any person allowing garbage, trash and rubbish to accumulate by failing to comply with the payment of the fees and charges fixed and assessed hereunder shall be liable to the full provisions of the law applicable to nuisance and upon the property owned by such person being declared a nuisance by reason of any unauthorized accumulation of garbage, trash and rubbish on any premises shall be subject to being tried for a nuisance as a violation of the terms of this chapter and upon conviction thereof in the municipal court of the city shall be fined or imprisoned, or both, within the discretion of the city recorder, and within the limits of the Charter of the city and the several amendments thereto.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
298:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction in the municipal court.
(Ord. 159 § 2 (part))
300:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "City of Sparta Anti-Litter Ordinance."
(Ord. 159 § 3 (part))
301:
For the purposes of this chapter the following terms, phrases, words and their derivations shall have the meaning given herein. The word shall is always mandatory and not merely directory.
Garbage means putrescible animal and vegetable wastes resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking and consumption of food.
Litter means garbage, refuse and rubbish as defined herein and all other waste material which, if thrown or deposited as herein prohibited, tends to create a danger to public health, safety and welfare.
Public receptacles means a receptacle or container placed by the city for public use in depositing litter. A receptacle commonly known as a "Dempster Dumpster" and placed by the city is declared to be a public receptacle.
Refuse means all putrescible and nonputrescible solid wastes (except body wastes), including garbage, rubbish, ashes, street cleanings, dead animals, and solid market and industrial wastes.
Rubbish means nonputrescible solid wastes consisting of both combustible and noncombustible wastes, such as paper, wrappings, cigarettes, cardboard, tin cans, wood, glass, bedding, crockery and similar materials.
(Ord. 159 § 3 (part))
302:
No person shall throw or deposit litter in or upon any street, sidewalk or other public place within the city except in public receptacles or in official city dumps; provided, however, lawn and yard clippings and leaves may be piled between the street right-of-way line and the actual street paving or sidewalk line if same are so placed as to prevent scattering and so as not to impede traffic or create a safety hazard.
(Ord. 159 § 3 (part))
303:
No person shall throw or deposit litter on any private property within the city, whether owned by such person or not, except that the owner or person in control of private property may maintain a metal fly-proof private receptacle(s) for collection in such a manner that litter will be prevented from being carried or deposited by the elements upon any street, sidewalk or other public place or upon any private property. When a public receptacle is available on private property, litter shall be deposited therein.
(Ord. 159 § 3 (part))
304:
Persons placing litter in public receptacles shall do so in such a manner as to prevent it from being carried or deposited by the elements upon any street, sidewalk or other public place or upon private property. Wooden and cardboard boxes and containers shall be disassembled or collapsed prior to placing same in a public receptacle, and all litter placed therein shall be reasonably compressed by the person placing same in the receptacle. The person opening the receptacle top or door shall securely close same prior to leaving the receptacle after a deposit has been made therein.
(Ord. 159 § 3 (part))
305:
Footnote 1:
Editor's note— Ord. No. 250, adopted Feb. 12, 2019, repealed the former Ch. 8.16, §§ 8.16.010—8.16.060, and enacted a new Ch. 8.16 as set out herein. The former Ch. 8.16 pertained to similar subject matter and derived from Ord. No. 206, §§ 1—6, adopted 1990.
306:
Anyone who violates a provision of this chapter shall, upon the first violation, receive a written warning. Upon a second violation, a person shall be subject to a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), such fine to be imposed at the discretion of the municipal judge.
(Ord. No. 250, 2-12-2019)
308:
It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully make, continue, or cause to be made or continued any excessive, unnecessary, or unusually loud noise which disturbs the peace or quiet of any neighborhood or which causes discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal sensitiveness residing within the city limits.
(Ord. No. 250, 2-12-2019)
309:
(a) General. It shall be unlawful for any person to create or cause to be created loud or unusual noises which are detrimental or annoying to reasonable people, including, without limitation, unusual loud disturbances such as loud music, and further including, without limitation, the following specifically prohibited conduct:
(1) The using, operating or permitting to be played, used or operated of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph or other machine or device for the producing of sound in such a manner as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of the neighboring inhabitants or at any time with louder volume than is necessary for convenient hearing for the persons who are in the room, vehicle or chamber in which such machine or device is operated and who are voluntary listeners thereto. The operation of any such set, instrument, phonograph, machine or device in such a manner as to be plainly audible at a distance of one hundred (100) feet from the building, structure or vehicle or, in the case of real property, beyond the property limits in which it is located, whichever is farthest, between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and between 12:00 midnight and 7:00 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday mornings shall be prima facie evidence of a violation of this section;
(2) The using, operating or permitting to be used, operated or played of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, loudspeaker, sound amplifier or other machine or device for the producing or reproducing of sound which is cast upon the public streets for the purpose of commercial advertising or which serves to attract the attention of the public to any building, structure or vehicle; or
(3) Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling or singing on the public streets, or private property, between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and between 12:00 midnight and 7:00 a.m. Saturday and Sunday mornings so as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort or repose of persons in any office, or in any dwelling, hotel or other type of residence, or of any reasonable persons in the vicinity.
(b) Construction equipment and activity. The operating of any equipment or the performing of any outside construction or repair work on buildings, structures, roads or projects within the city between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., unless a permit for such construction or repair work between such hours has been obtained from the police chief or city clerk.
(c) Exhausts. The discharging into the open air of the exhaust of any internal combustion engine, motor boat, or motor vehicle, except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom.
(d) Animals and birds. The keeping of any animal or bird which by frequent or continuous barking, chirping, or other means of communication disturbs the comfort or repose of the reasonable people who reside in the residential neighborhood.
(e) Vehicle repair in residential areas. The repairing, rebuilding, or testing of any motor vehicle between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. within any residential area in such a manner as to disturb the peace, quiet, and comfort of the residents of the area.
(f) Schools, courts, churches, hospitals. The creating of any excessive noise on any street adjacent to any school, institution of learning, church, or court while the same are in use, or adjacent to any hospital, which unreasonably interferes with the working of such institution, or which disturbs or unduly annoys patients in the hospital, provided conspicuous signs are displayed in such streets indicating that the same is a school, hospital, or court street.
(g) Hawkers and peddlers. The selling of anything by outcry within the residential areas of the city, except at licensed sporting events, parades, fairs, circuses, and other similar licensed public entertainment events.
(h) Drums. The using of any drum or other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention by the creation of noise within the city, unless a permit for such use has been obtained from the city clerk or police chief.
(i) Compression and engine brakes. It shall be unlawful for any person in actual physical control of a motor vehicle, including, but not limited to a truck or tractor-trailer truck, to use an engine brake or compression brakes while traveling along the streets of the city unless such engine brake or compression brake is used solely to affect an emergency stop of the motor vehicle. Upon conviction in a court of competent jurisdiction, the fine for a violation of this subsection shall not be for less than five hundred dollars ($500.00) in addition to any other penalties that may be authorized by law or ordinance.
For purposes of this subsection (i) the following definitions shall apply:
Compression brake is any device which, by the release of compressed air within an engine cylinder prior to the ignition of fuel therein, results in the slowing of said vehicle and/or braking without the use of wheel brakes, said devices commonly being referred to as "Jacobs brakes," "Jake brakes," "dynamic brake," "C-brake," or "Paccar brake."
Engine brake is any device which, by the release of compressed air within an engine cylinder prior to the ignition of fuel therein, results in the slowing of said vehicle and/or braking without the use of wheel brakes, said devices commonly being referred to as "Jacobs brakes," "Jake brakes," "dynamic brake," "C-brake," or "Paccar brake."

This Agreement made and entered into as of the 1st day of May, 1991, by, between and among the City of Greensboro, Georgia, the City of Sparta, Georgia and the City of Union Point, Georgia, each a municipal corporation validly created and existing under the laws of the State of Georgia, and Glascock County, Georgia, Greene County, Georgia, Hancock County, Georgia, Lincoln County, Georgia, Taliaferro County, Georgia, Warren County, Georgia, and Wilkes County, Georgia, each a political subdivision validly created and existing under the laws of the State of Georgia;

WHEREAS, after diligent study and review, each Participant has also determined that it is in the best interest of the citizens of that Participant for each of the Participants to enter into an Agreement with the other Participants providing for the activation of the Authority and the appointment of the Board of Directors of the Authority under the terms of the Act and to provide for the initial operation of the Authority and the Authority's preliminary role in studying and planning for possible future projects of the Authority and for the management of the Participants' solid waste needs; and
WHEREAS, Art. 9, Section 3, Par. 1 of the Constitution of the State of Georgia provides, in pertinent part, that any county, municipality or other political subdivision of the State of Georgia may contract for any period not exceeding fifty (50) years with each other or with any public agency, public corporation, or public authority for joint services, for the provision of services, or for the joint or separate use of facilities or equipment for such activities, services or facilities which the county, municipality or public authority is authorized by law to undertake or provide;

A. Any person, persons or groups desiring to stage a parade, demonstration or assembly, or engage in picketing, shall make application for a permit to the city of Sparta not later than two (2) weeks prior to the day that such proposed activity is intended to be staged or carried out. Such application shall be filed with the city clerk, who shall forward the same to the mayor and council. Such permit shall be granted by the mayor and council, but the mayor and council shall be empowered to determine and reasonably restrict the time and duration of the proposed activity, the number of units or automobiles to be involved, the number of persons to participate in such activity, and the streets or locations where such activity shall be allowed, so as not to impair the safety and convenience of the public generally, after giving due consideration to the same.
B. An application and permit shall be required for each such activity; provided, however, only one (1) application and permit shall be required for each proposed parade, demonstration, assembly, or picketing site and course of picketing.

364:
All such activities shall be conducted under the supervision of the person or persons making application for the same, and shall be conducted in a peaceable and orderly manner in compliance with the laws and ordinance applicable thereto.
(Ord. 163 (part))
365:
In the conduct of such activities, no signs, shields or banners shall be placed or carried by any person upon the sidewalks of this city that extend beyond the width of the person's body or extend more than twenty-four (24) inches above the person's head; and persons carrying any signs, shields or banners shall be at least ten (10) feet apart, shall not stand or loiter in front of any doorway, driveway or street intersection, and shall not interfere with the general flow of traffic, whether pedestrian or vehicular.
(Ord. 163 (part))
366:
For the purpose of this chapter, a parade is defined as "any procession, excepting funerals containing twenty-five (25) or more persons or five (5) or more vehicles"; and for the purposes of this chapter, an assembly is defined as "a crowd of more than ten (10) persons standing, congregated or assembled upon any of the sidewalks or streets or other public property in the city." For the purposes of this chapter, the terms demonstration and picketing shall be given their usual meaning, considering the context in which they are herein used.
(Ord. 163 (part))
369:
The mayor and council shall act upon the application for a parade permit as soon as possible after receiving it. If the mayor and council disapproves the application, the clerk of the city shall notify the applicant immediately, stating the reasons for the denial of the permit.

370:
Any person aggrieved shall have the right to appeal the denial of a parade permit to the mayor and council. The aggrieved shall request a meeting time and place of the clerk of the city.
(Ord. 163 § 4)
371:
The mayor and council, in denying the application for a parade permit, shall be empowered to authorize the conduct of the parade on a date, at a time, or over a route different from that named by the applicant. An applicant desiring to accept an alternate permit shall submit a written notice of acceptance with the clerk of the city. Any alternate parade permit shall conform to the requirements of and shall have the effect of a parade permit under this chapter.

373:

374:

D. Under normal conditions the consumer will be notified of any anticipated interruptions of service by the city of Sparta.
(Ord. 210 § 6, 2000: Ord. 205 § 6)
385:
A. Duly authorized agents of the city of Sparta shall have access at all hours to the premises of the consumer for the purpose of installing or removing city property, inspecting piping, reading and testing meters, or for any other purpose in connection with the water service and its facilities, and the sewer service and its facilities.
B. Extensions to the system shall be made only when the consumer shall grant or convey, or shall cause to be granted or conveyed, to the city of Sparta a permanent easement of right-of-way across any property traversed by the water or sewer lines.
(Ord. 210 § 8, 2000: Ord. 205 § 8)
386:
Not less than three (3) days notice must be given, in person or in writing, at the City Hall of the city of Sparta to discontinue water and sewer service or to change occupancy. The outgoing party shall be responsible for all water consumed up to the time of departure or the time specified for departure, whichever period is longer. The new occupant shall apply for water service within forty-eight (48) hours after occupying the premises and failure to do so will make him liable for paying for the water consumed since the last meter reading.
(Ord. 210 § 9, 2000: Ord. 205 § 9)
387:
Bills to customer for water and sewer service shall be mailed out on such day or days each month as may be determined as desirable by the city. The failure of water and/or sewer users to pay charges duly imposed shall result in the automatic imposition of the following penalties:
A. Nonpayment within ten (10) days from the due date will be subject to a penalty of ten (10) percent of the delinquent account.
B. Nonpayment within twenty (20) days from the date due will result in the water being shut off from the water user's property.
C. Nonpayment for sixty (60) days after original billing date will allow the city, in addition to all other rights and remedies, to terminate agreement, and in such event, the water user shall not be entitled to receive, nor the city obligated to supply, any water under this agreement.
D. The city clerk or other duly authorized collector of water and sewer charges shall, after the failure of any person or entity to pay delinquent water and sewer bills and the water department has certified that other methods of collection are ineffective, place a fi. fa. on the property where service was received and shall maintain a docket on delinquent water and sewer bills which shall be available for examination. In addition to any delinquent water and sewer bills, the city clerk is authorized to charge the property owner any costs for the execution of the fi. fa. and the maintenance of the docket.
E. In all instances where the water and sewer customer is not the record owner of the property, the city clerk must mail a copy of the delinquent notice to the record owner and said record owner must be given at least thirty (30) days to resolve any delinquency before the city clerk may file a fi. fa.
F. Customers that have a past due balance after disconnection are subject to being referred to collection agencies and are required to pay for postage, second notices, collection fees, court processing fees, and attorney fees.
Water and sewer service shall not be reconnected until customer's delinquent bill, including penalty and disconnection charges, have been paid in full. Should such customer thereafter desire to be reconnected to the water and sewer system, a reconnection charge of ten dollars ($10.00) shall be collected. Bills shall be paid at the City Hall of city of Sparta and a failure to receive bills and notices shall not prevent such bills from becoming delinquent nor relieve the consumer from payment of same.
(Ord. 220, 2007; Ord. 211, 2004; Ord. 210 § 10, 2000: Ord. 205 § 10)
389:

Such claim, if made after the bill has become delinquent, shall not be effective in preventing discontinuance of service as heretofore provided. The consumer may pay such bill under protest and said payment shall not prejudice his claim.
A. The city will make a special water meter reading at the request of a consumer for a fee of three dollars ($3.00); provided, however, that if such special reading discloses that the meter was over-read, no charge will be made.
B. Water meters will be tested at the request of the consumer upon payment to the city of the actual costs of making the test (minimum ten dollars ($10.00)); provided, however, that if the meter is found to over-register beyond three (3) percent of the correct volume, no charge will be made.
C. If the seal of a meter is broken by other than the city's representative or if the meter fails to register correctly or is stopped for any cause, the consumer shall pay an amount estimated from the record of his previous bills and/or from other proper data.
(Ord. 210 § 12, 2000: Ord. 205 § 12)
390:
From and after the passage of the ordinance codified in this chapter, it shall be required that all residences, business establishments and other structures having a wastewater discharge within the city limits of the city of Sparta to connect onto the city's central sewer system where said structure is within two hundred (200) feet of said sewer line. Said connection shall be made within sixty (60) days of availability of sewer service.
All new construction within the city limits of the city of Sparta within two hundred (200) feet of the city's sewer line shall also be required to connect onto said system.
(Ord. 210 § 13, 2000: Ord. 205 § 13)

Each day's violation shall be deemed a separate violation.
